procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism registers the factory (requires the factory to be located outside a free zone, a MoIAT industrial licence, and a MoIAT letter confirming 40% domestic value added; takes about 3 working days).
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The exporter prepares the application documents: proof of factory registration, the commercial invoice, and for a trading exporter, the factory's purchase invoice.
The exporter logs in to the ministry e-services portal, chooses the Certificate of Origin for India service, fills in the application form, uploads the required documents, and pays the fee online.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade charges a certificate fee of AED 50 (band: invoice value up to AED 100000).
The exporter submits the application and receives approval, or a return with comments to correct, then prints the approved certificate.
The competent authority issues the certificate prior to, at, or within five working days of the date of exportation.
The certificate is valid for twelve months from the date of issue and covers only one import.
The exporter ensures the goods are shipped directly from the UAE to India; if in transit, only under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading, storage or similar.
The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry, holds origin information under CAROTAR 2020, and keeps supporting documents for at least five years from filing.
The exporter keeps origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least five years starting from the end of the calendar year of the date of issue.

caveats.note: The factory is declared in a free zone: likely not eligible for the ministry's factory registration; confirm with the ministry.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
'+' in the rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass); the agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
The duty estimate is on the shipment value given; India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only; IGST, GST compensation cess, the Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India; confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
The Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) is likely charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text on it was found).
Anti-dumping and safeguard duties likely still apply (no CEPA exemption from them was found).
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum for record keeping; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.
The issuing authority may apply risk management, including asking for detailed cost sheets and visiting the factory.
